# Extracting tetralayer-graphene stacking order from magnetotransport — a survey

*A grounded review of how to distinguish the tetralayer (N = 4) graphene
stacking orders — ABAB (Bernal), ABCA (rhombohedral), ABCB (mixed) — by
transport, and the measurement method it motivates. Synthesises four ingested
references — Min–MacDonald 2008 (`papers/0711.4333/paper.md`, chiral
decomposition), Koshino–McCann 2011 (`papers/1104.0794/paper.md`,
full-parameter Bernal-N LLs), Grushina et al. 2015
(`papers/1501.06764/paper.md`, Bernal-4L experiment), Kalantre et al. 2026
(`papers/2606.05356/paper.md`, R4G fermiology + model). Companion to the
trilayer survey (`stacking-extraction-survey.md`), whose method framework —
F_L combinatorics, scale pinning, harmonic screen, per-channel reads — carries
over unchanged; this survey carries only what is N = 4-specific. The
operational decision procedure lives in
`recipes/investigations/tetralayer-stacking-fs-count.md`.*

> **Provenance and strength conventions** (`recipes/STYLE.md`): **paper-data**
> · **citation** · **our-model** · **heuristic**; calls use **decisive ·
> strong · weak · consistent-with · uninformative**.

---

## 1. The three stackings and their decomposition

2^(N−2) = 4 raw sequences collapse to **three distinct tetralayer orders**
(theory-paper, `papers/0711.4333` Table I; ABCB ≡ ABAC read end-to-end):

| Stacking | Chiral blocks | Low-energy bands | CNP at D = 0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ABAB** (Bernal) | J = 2 ⊕ 2 | two bilayer-like parabolic pairs, masses ∝ λγ₁ with λ = 1.618 / 0.618 | semimetallic; e–h overlap structure at γ₂ scale; interaction gap in ultraclean devices (§5) |
| **ABCA** (rhombohedral) | J = 4 | single quartic (k⁴ + trigonal warping) flat-bottomed band | gapless; gaps under D |
| **ABCB** (mixed, metastable) | J = 3 ⊕ 1 | cubic (k³) + linear (k) Dirac-like pair | **intrinsic** gap ≈ 9 meV (citation: Wirth et al., arXiv:2203.07971 — not yet ingested) |

Two symmetry facts with consequences (theory-paper, `papers/1104.0794`):
even-N Bernal has **no mirror plane**, so ABAB's two bilayer blocks are mixed
by γ₂/γ₅ even at D = 0 — the two-Fermi-surface picture is exact only above
the ~20 meV remote-hopping scale, and inter-block magnetic breakdown is
symmetry-allowed (unlike trilayer's parity-protected ML/BL). Even-N *does*
have inversion symmetry, forcing **valley degeneracy** of the ABAB spectrum
at D = 0 (trilayer's low LLs valley-split; ABAB's do not until D breaks
inversion).

## 2. Primary discriminator — the FS count against F_L

Same read as the trilayer method: enumerate resolved SdH tones, screen
harmonics, and match the peak *set* against the Luttinger frequency
F_L = (h/4e)·n (g = 4 while degeneracies are unbroken). The N = 4 templates:

- **ABCA → a singleton at F_L.** One post-cascade pocket carries the full
  density. Trigonal-warping Lifshitz structure is confined to low density
  (citation: the cascade scale shrinks with N vs the trilayer ~10¹¹ cm⁻²;
  quantitative D = 0 boundaries pending our-model). At the ~10¹² operating
  density: one surface.
- **ABAB → a pair partitioning F_L at ≈ 0.72 / 0.28.** Parabolic bands at a
  shared E_F populate ∝ mass, and the block masses scale with the effective
  couplings λ₃γ₁ / λ₁γ₁ → density (and frequency) ratio λ₃/λ₁ = φ² ≈ 2.62
  (theory-paper, `papers/1104.0794`). That is the parabolic
  (decomposition-limit) value; the full model distorts it both ways —
  γ₂-scale band-bottom offsets at low |n|, non-parabolicity at high |n| —
  and the design numbers are its F(n) table (our-model,
  `models/tetralayer_fs_count`). Two exception regimes: at **low electron
  density** the light pocket nearly empties (0.6 T at +1×10¹²) and the heavy
  tone rides at ≈ 0.95·F_L — the one regime where ABAB genuinely mimics an
  ABCA singleton within the scale prior; on the **near-CNP hole side** the
  semimetal overlap leaves the pair close and balanced ([4.4, 5.9] T at
  −1×10¹²) — a beat, not two resolved tones, on a short 1/B record. Both
  wash out by |n| ≳ 2–3×10¹².
- **ABCB → a pair with a Dirac partner.** Cubic main tone + linear-band
  small tone over the intrinsic gap (theory-paper `papers/0711.4333`;
  magnitude/partition citation-grade until modeled). The J = 1 velocity is
  renormalized below the monolayer value — do not fit the small tone with a
  pristine-Dirac slope.

**Why this is an easier read than the trilayer case**: the trilayer
discriminator hinges on a small (few-%–17%) ML tone because ABA's dominant
tone nearly coincides with ABC's singleton. At N = 4 and design densities
|n| ≳ 2–3×10¹² the dominant tones themselves separate — ABAB's biggest tone
sits at ≈ 0.72–0.79·F_L, well off the ABCA singleton at F_L — and the ABAB
partner tone carries ~21–28% of F_L. Presence *and* position of the dominant
tone discriminate, with the partner tone and Luttinger partition as
confirmation. The low-|n| exception regimes above are where the advantage
evaporates — design around them.

Carried over unchanged from the trilayer method (see that survey and recipe):
pin the global scale on the whole peak set first; classify on frequencies,
never amplitudes; screen harmonics by integer multiples + n-dependence; read
each Rxx channel separately (mosaic flakes); and the **F_L sum-tone
confound** — an ABAB pair's breakdown/mixing tone lands at f₁+f₂ = F_L and
mimics the ABCA singleton. Note the confound is *more* live at N = 4: ABAB
inter-block breakdown is symmetry-allowed (§1), so the F_L-tone origin
discrimination (B-window split, grid-change reproduction, per-branch LK mass)
is mandatory before any singleton call.

**LK mass split is stronger at N = 4** (theory-paper + heuristic): the ABAB
pair's masses differ by φ² ≈ 2.6× (≈ 0.05 vs 0.02 m_e importing the bilayer
mass scale — heuristic, ~30% error bar), so per-branch LK masses cleanly
separate two genuine bands from one band + artifact. Both ABAB branches are
parabolic — there is **no Dirac-vs-parabolic shape contrast** as in trilayer;
branch labeling comes from the frequency ratio and mass ratio. ABCB restores
a light Dirac partner (renormalized velocity, §2).

## 3. Displacement field

D ≈ 0 remains the operating point. Responses diverge by stacking
(theory-paper + citation): **ABCA** opens/deepens a CNP gap with D (standard
rhombohedral Mexican-hat behavior; the R4G phase diagram in
`papers/2606.05356` fig1). **ABAB** stays unGapped as a whole — D breaks
inversion, splits valleys (observed in the light subband only; citation:
PRB 106, L161405 — not yet ingested) and reshapes the e–h overlap, and D
hybridizes the two blocks on top of the intrinsic γ₂ mixing. **ABCB** starts
gapped at D = 0. A quantitative small-D robustness statement for the ABAB
pair (the analog of the trilayer Δ₁² argument) is pending our-model — until
then treat "D ≈ 0, small residual D harmless" as heuristic at N = 4.

## 4. High-field face — the trilayer Streda offset does NOT carry

The chirality sum rule ΣJ = N makes the zero-LL count and the CNP Hall jump
**stacking-blind within a layer number**: every tetralayer stacking has 16
zero-energy LLs and σ_xy jumping 16 e²/h across neutrality, first plateaus
ν = ±8, 12, 16 (theory-paper, `papers/0711.4333`; measured for ABAB —
paper-data, `papers/1501.06764`). There is **no tetralayer analog of the
ABA-vs-ABC sequence-offset discriminator**; a ν = 8,12,16 ladder identifies
the *layer number*, not the stacking.

What remains at high field is LL **fine structure** (theory-paper,
`papers/1104.0794`): ABAB = two interleaved bilayer ladders (zero-mode
groups offset by 2|γ₂|/√5 ≈ 18 meV, mod-3 anticrossings, valley-degenerate,
4e²/h steps) vs ABCA = a single bunched B²-like ladder vs ABCB = B^{3/2} +
B^{1/2} ladders. Currently **qualitative** — no validated 4L LL model in the
corpus; the minimal chiral model is invalid at laboratory fields
(`papers/0711.4333`, validity domain), so any future quantitative use goes
through full-parameter models. Treat high-field structure as a complement,
weight ≤ weak, until modeled.

## 5. Complementary discriminators — and why CNP magnitude is weaker than at N = 3

An insulating CNP in a tetralayer has **three** candidate parents:

1. **ABCB intrinsic gap** (~9 meV, citation);
2. **ABCA under finite D** (paper-data, `papers/2606.05356`);
3. **ABAB interaction-driven insulator at D = 0** — ultraclean Bernal 4L
   gaps at neutrality with no displacement field (E_A ≈ 15 K, |n| <
   3×10¹⁰ cm⁻²; paper-data, `papers/1501.06764`). Requires suspended-grade
   cleanliness to *resolve*, so its absence is uninformative at ordinary n*.

CNP-resistance behavior is therefore **consistent-with at best, never the
call**, on top of the domain/series-path shunting confound that already
weakens it at N = 3 (trilayer survey §5, carries unchanged). Frequency
content is untouched by all three states (they live within ~10¹⁰–10¹¹ cm⁻²
of neutrality); the FS count at |n| ~ 10¹² is the discriminator.

## 6. Isospin / correlated-phase caveat — scoped by the R4G reference

R4G hosts documented Onsager-defeating states — but concentrated at **large
|D| and low n near the flat-band vHS** (paper-data, `papers/2606.05356`:
flavor cascade, multitone state). At D ≈ 0 and |n| ≳ 10¹² the same device
shows the clean symmetric-metal read (f_ν = n_SdH/n = 1/4, its fig s21), and
symmetry-broken states in tetralayers develop only at sub-kelvin
temperatures (paper-data: R4G cascade at 28 mK; ABAB QH symmetry breaking
below ~1 K, `papers/1501.06764`) — at kelvin-scale electron temperatures
the symmetric 4-fold metal is the expected state at the operating point
(heuristic). **Verify, don't assume**: F_L = (h/4e)·n already encodes g = 4,
so the tone positions themselves audit the degeneracy — a peak set sitting
at 2× or 4× its g = 4-predicted position (after the scale is pinned on the
full set) reads as g = 2 / g = 1 flavor polarization, which suspends the
g = 4 combinatorics rather than being "supra-F_L" evidence.

## 7. Absolute layer number — the cross-check runs both ways

Optical-contrast/Raman N-assignment can misassign the absolute layer count
while resolving relative steps well. The FS count itself audits N: a peak
set matching neither 4L template should raise **adjacent-N misassignment**
(trilayer's ML+BL pair or pentalayer's 2+2+1 / J=5 structures) before exotic
explanations. Decisive independent N-ID where needed: magneto-Raman G-band
anticrossings (paper-data, `papers/1501.06764` — 4L resonances at 5.8, 7.8,
12 T, distinct from 3L/5L, room-T-capable).

## 8. Forward models and pipeline

- **`models/tetralayer_fs_count/`** (our-model): sequence-parameterized
  2n×2n solver — **ABAB** SWMcC with the Koshino–McCann graphite set
  (`papers/1104.0794`, γ₃ = 0, radial), **ABCA** 8-band continuum with the
  Kalantre Set-1 parameters (`papers/2606.05356` S15, γ₃ ON, 2D grid, u_D
  supported), **ABCB** qualitative via the mixed-linkage builder. Gates
  passing (residuals in its README): decomposition limit (λ = 0.618/1.618,
  partition → 0.7236), Luttinger both signs (≤ 0.015 T), Eq.-18 vHS
  (analytic 42.8 meV vs numerical 43), Lifshitz cascade topology vs S29
  (boundaries qualitative, ~2–4× the digitization), ABA/ABC backtest vs the
  frozen trilayer model (≤ 0.17%), m\* identities. Its README's F(n)/m\*(n)
  key table is the design authority for the feasibility pass. Outstanding:
  independent ABCA cross-validation against `RhombohedralGrapheneLandau.jl`
  (N-layer rhombohedral julia package; dev-side only, never a session
  dependency).
- **4L LL models**: not built; §4 stays qualitative.
- **SdH-FFT pipeline**: unchanged from the trilayer bundle
  (`models/trilayer_fs_count/rmg-fft-snapshot/`), independently corroborated
  by the R4G paper's robustness supplement (detrend in B *before*
  interpolating to 1/B; `papers/2606.05356` s13 discussion).

## 9. Summary — what the investigation operationalises

The stacking call rests on the **peak set against F_L**: ABAB a 0.72/0.28
pair (φ²-split LK masses, symmetry-allowed breakdown sum-tone at F_L), ABCA
a singleton at F_L, ABCB a cubic+Dirac pair over an intrinsic gap
[citation-grade]. Dominant tones separate by ~28% of F_L — a structurally
easier read than trilayer's small-tone hunt — with the Luttinger partition,
per-branch LK masses, and F_L-tone origin discrimination as the
confirmation battery — with the low-|n| exception regimes (§2) designed
around using the model's F(n) table. High-field sequence offsets are
unavailable at N = 4 (chirality sum rule); CNP magnitude carries three
confounded parents; both are demoted to weak complements. Open items: the
julia cross-validation and S29 quantitative reconciliation (model README),
ingesting Wirth et al. (ABCB) and PRB 106 L161405 (ABAB e–h hybridization /
valley splitting) if their reads become load-bearing, and the 4L LL models.

## What
2D map of carrier density × magnetic field at fixed displacement field: `mag.field` as the **slow** axis of a `multimegasweep`, with a paired-(k_tg, k_bg) n-line (fixed D, via `calculate_gate_voltages(ns, Ds, dtg=..., dbg=...)`) as the **fast** axis:
```python
s.multimegasweep([mag.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs], slow_delay=1, fast_delay=0.9)
```
Field is slow because gates are cheap to retrace and the magnet is not — the magnet ramps once, monotonically, across the whole fan. Every lock-in X/P read at each grid point. Analysis side plots B vs n (`pcolormesh`) per contact pair and overlays Středa lines (see Verify). Distinct from its two neighbors: `field-sweep-1d` is one gate point with full B-axis density; `gatemap-in-field` is the full 2D gate plane at a *single* B. The fan trades both for the (n, B) plane — the only measurement that resolves how gapped states *disperse* with field.

## When
Three triggers, in rough campaign order:
- **Oscillation check** — a `field-sweep-1d` or `gatemap-in-field` showed quantum-oscillation-like wiggles and you need to know if they're real. The corpus idiom is literally named for this: RPL_19's "Small fan to check if oscillations are real" (a 161 × 151 fan after an effective-mass series kept hinting at SdH). A feature that moves systematically across the n-line as B steps is physics; one that doesn't is noise or gate drift.
- **State classification** — a map shows a vanishing-ρxx region (or a busy set of dips) and the discriminating question is whether the features disperse. This is the classification backbone of an FQAH/SC-style campaign (arXiv 2504.06972: ρxx(ν_h, B) fans + Středa fits are how (R/F/I)QAH states were separated from the SC region).
- **Calibration** — SdH/LL frequency vs n gives cap ratios independently of the CNP-slope method, and for a moiré device the fan anchors the moiré density n_M. The extraction is `cap-ratio-calibration`'s job (deferred — recipe not yet written); the fan is its input data.

Prerequisites are `nD-map`'s plus a field-verified magnet: cap ratios `dtg`/`dbg` must be trusted (the fast axis is a line in (n, D) — wrong caps tilt it), and the field source must be live (Yokogawa cache seeded after kernel restart, AMI430 in operating mode — see `field-sweep-1d` plumbing notes).

## Why
A dip in ρxx at one B value is ambiguous — gap, SC, contact artifact, density wobble. The same dip tracked across a fan is nearly unambiguous: a gapped state at fixed filling traces a straight line in (n, B) whose slope *is* its Chern number (Středa: dn/dB = C·e/h), an SC pocket sits at fixed n and dies at moderate B without dispersing, and quantum oscillations fan out with 1/B periodicity that yields the Fermi-surface area. One measurement, three discriminations, plus calibration for free.

The cost is real: these are the most expensive sweeps in the corpus. Reference wall-clocks *(our-measurement, toploader, non-blocking-magnet era — the formula below them omits the traverse term; do not carry these numbers to another rig untagged)*: RPL_10's 101 B × 101 n fan at `slow_delay=30, fast_delay=1` took **4.3 h** (file 156); the 351 × 251 version took **27.8 h** (file 159); RPL_19's 161 × 151 at `fast_delay=0.6` took **5.5 h** (file 1776 — Aaron's own `# 1776, took 5.5 hours` annotation propagates through later fan cells); the 441 × 231 fan to 5 T took **30.1 h** (file 1840). Aaron's inline arithmetic (`(351*501)/(201*151)*3` in 20260124 cell 134) is the toploader-era form.

**Estimate before you run — the full cost model**: wall-clock = **field-traverse time + N_rows × (row turnaround + N_fast × per-point time)**. Which term dominates is a rig property, not a constant of nature: **if the field source is ramp-rate-limited and the set call blocks** (check the rig card for whether yours is), the traverse term is fixed by the B-span alone — **finer B steps cost only row turnaround, and coarsening B buys aliasing, not time**. Traverses come in two species, priced differently: a **bare ramp** moves at the magnet's ramp rate; a **measured traverse** (the same leg recorded as a sweep) moves at an effective rate degraded by per-point overhead. A "free" measured ramp-down is usually still worth taking — it buys data for wall-clock — but it is not free: price it at the measured rate, from the rig card's Timing rules (`rig_card.md`), never the bare one. Calibrate row turnaround and per-point time from this session's own first sweeps; inherited timing constants carry a provenance tag and the conditions they were measured under, or they are guesses.

## Recipe
1. Pick the n-window and fixed D from the map that motivated the fan, and decide the B span. Corpus shapes: oscillation check 0.9 → 2.5 T over a 151-pt n-line; classification fan 0 → 2.5 T, 251 × 151; deep fan 0.6 → 5 T, 441 × 231; high-field 5 → 12 T, 351 × 201. Start coarse (≤200 B steps, ≤151 n points); zoom only on confirmed structure. **Grid Nyquist check, both axes, at design time**: against the finest expected feature spacing in the analysis window. The **B-axis** check depends on the read: a **Středa/SC fan** (dip positions, no FFT) samples uniform in B, may start at 0, and needs ≥2 (prefer 3) rows per LL period ΔB ≈ (g·e/h)·B²/n (g = 4 for spin×valley) at the **lowest-B, highest-n corner**; a **per-column SdH-FFT fan** samples uniform in 1/B (`field_invB`, B_lo > 0) and needs Δ(1/B) ≤ 1/(2·F) (prefer 1/3) at the highest n, F = (h/4e)·n. The **n-axis** check (both): ray spacing Δn = g·(e/h)·B at the lowest B you intend to read, same ≥2 floor. For a **per-column SdH-FFT fan** also compute the resolution **δF = 1/(1/B_onset − 1/B_max)** against the tones the claim must separate (~2·δF to trust a split) — δF is set by the record above onset, not by grid density; if it can't separate the tones, redesign the window or the density, don't densify. An undersampled axis produces in-data aliasing that mimics curved structure and survives re-plotting; no post-hoc check fully recovers it. "Start coarse" applies to the *window*, never below the Nyquist floor of the structure you intend to claim — and where the cost model says fine B is nearly free (blocking ramp-limited magnets), take it. **Re-run this check whenever n_max changes — never inherit the field sampling across fans.** The requirement tightens with n (Δ(1/B) ∝ 1/n, ΔB ∝ B²/n), so a sampling fine enough for an n≤4 fan undersamples an n=10 firming fan (our-measurement, QC0426/VTI 2026-06-14, uniform-B at ΔB=0.1 T: 2.2 rows/period at n=4 but only 1.5 — under the ≥2 floor — at n=10, B=4 T, where a spurious high-n second pocket appeared and had to be killed post-hoc). Where the rig makes fine B *not* free (measurement-dominated fans, e.g. a non-blocking-magnet rig at >1 s/pt — check the cost model), buy the high-n Nyquist floor by **trimming n-points or flooring the high-n claim at B ≥ 5–6 T**, not by coarsening the field sampling. **Dynamic-range check, at design time**: a fan reads through one *fixed* sensitivity, so the scale must clear the **global worst corner**, structurally **low n × high B** — R ∝ 1/n on the gate axis stacks with the B-axis MR (10–100× zero-field). Size full-scale with **headroom, not precision** — saturation is the asymmetric failure: **better to lose low-resistance resolution than saturate** (expert practice). Set the scale comfortably above I_bias·R(n_min, B_max), anchoring R_max from a spot-check/CNP R-anchor × the **low-n** MR factor (MR grows toward CNP; a high-|n| factor under-sizes the corner — our-measurement). **Clipping distorts, it does not drop**: a railed column is flat-topped → harmonics + corrupted bg-subtraction across its whole FFT, unrecoverable by any B-window (the clean data sits at low B, the clip at high B). **Cost-floor check, at design time**: propose **exactly one** fan — the cheapest that clears the two checks above and delivers the claim. Compute `N_B · N_n · t_pt` and set each lever to its floor. **Do not offer a cheaper alternative or defer the trim to the operator — the floored design *is* the proposal.** Levers, in order: (1) **`B_lo` = the measured onset from `hera.analysis.sdh_onset(R, B).onset_b` — compute it, do not eyeball it** (sub-onset rows are background, not signal; a too-low `B_lo` inflates both the 1/B span and the n-axis Nyquist, and eyeballed onsets run systematically too low). If the carrying tone is `censored`, the spot-check record never captured the onset — `onset_b` is that record's low edge, a valid lower bound for `B_lo`; a cheap low-field extension pins it before committing a long fan. `SdhOnsetError` means no usable oscillations — re-examine the spot check, do not guess a `B_lo`; (2) **`n_max` = the validity window of the claim**; (3) `N_n` = its ray-Nyquist floor at `B_lo`; (4) `B_max` = the claim (more periods sharpen tones, but `B_max` past what the claim needs is just cost). `n_max` is the most expensive lever — out-of-validity it pays on *both* `N_B` and `N_n` (`Δ(1/B) ∝ 1/n_max`). State the computed `N_B`, `N_n`, and wall-clock in the proposal.
2. Build the fast axis: `ns = np.linspace(n_hi, n_lo, N); Ds = D0 * np.ones(len(ns)); Vtgs, Vbgs = calculate_gate_voltages(ns, Ds, dtg=..., dbg=...)`. A non-uniform n-vector is legitimate when you know where the action is — RPL_19's elevated-T fan stitches `np.hstack((n1, n2, n3))` with the dense segment over the CSC window and coarse segments elsewhere, with `#`-comments labeling each segment (20260124 cell 239).
3. Set the sensitivity (from the step-1 dynamic-range check) and time constant as an explicit pre-cell, fixed for the whole fan. RPL_19/20260217 cell 124 is the idiom: `sr830_N.sensitivity(10e-3)`, `sr830_N.time_constant(300e-3)`. Excitation: Aaron runs 1 V (graphene-scale) and bumps to 2.5 V for 12 T work; on a fragile-state device (FQAH/SC, arXiv 2504.06972's 1 nA cap) respect the device-card excitation ceiling instead — the states you're classifying wash out if heated.
4. Build the slow field axis: a **per-column SdH-FFT fan** uses `B_vec = field_invB(B_start, B_end, N)` (uniform in 1/B, both > 0); a **Středa/SC fan** uses `np.linspace` and may start at 0. Position the magnet at the fan's start field and let it settle: `s.ramp(mag.field, B_start)` then `time.sleep(600)` for multi-tesla positioning (RPL_19/20260217 cells 88/94), `time.sleep(30)` at ~1 T (RPL_10), `time.sleep(5*60)` at 0.6 T (20260124 cell 235). Plan the direction (endpoint order) so the fan *starts* where the magnet already is and *ends* where the next measurement needs it — never re-traverse. The elevated-T fan covers ±5 T as four chained segments (5→0.6, 0.6→0, 0→−0.6, −0.6→−5; 20260124 cells 239–242), each starting where the last ended.
5. Build `s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)`. `s.add_comment('landau-fan')` then a structured tag: `s.add_comment(f'D = {D0} V/nm, n = {n_lo} to {n_hi}, B = {B_start} to {B_end} T')`, plus `s.add_comment(grab_metadata())` where available. **Watch out** — RPL_10's fans carry exemplary comments (`'MC4, Vsi = -20V, quantum oscillations, D = 0.31 V/nm, n = -2.9 to -2.1, B = 1 to 0 T'`); RPL_19's fan cells carry *none* (files 1776/1840 have empty `comments`) — only a stale `# 1776` Python comment. The recipe asks for the RPL_10 discipline.
6. `s.ramp(sr830_1.amplitude, A)`, `s.ramp(k_si.volt, V_si)`, `s.ramp(bias_voltage.volt, 0)` if present. `fp` temperature(s) and every lock-in X/P; `plot` gate currents for live leakage (`s.plot(k_bg.volt, k_bg.curr)`, `s.plot('time', k_tg.curr)`, `s.plot('time', k_si.curr)` — RPL_19 fan idiom; note `fp` of gate currents is often omitted here, so leakage lands in the live plot but *not* in the TSV).
7. The sweep (step 0 call above). Delay band in the corpus: `slow_delay=1` (gates retrace during it; the field step itself is rate-limited by the magnet), `fast_delay` ≈ 4τ default — a Středa/dispersion fan tolerates the uniform fast-axis lag like a slope; ~6τ when the n-axis carries the extracted signal (per-column SdH FFT, or coarse n), where the lag distorts it, with denser n trading against the dwell.
8. Park gates (`k_bg.volt(0); k_tg.volt(0)`), decide the field endpoint deliberately (leave it for a follow-up fan, `s.ramp(mag.field, 0)`, or ride home as a measured traverse — a free `field-sweep-1d`, priced at the measured rate per the Why cost model), and ping (`alerts.discord('🐍jobs done🐍')`) — at 5–30 h these runs outlive operator attention spans.

## Verify
Disk-side checks, then the Středa read. The fan is unrolled into flat rows; the slow column is `magnet_field`.

```python
from hera.analysis import open_run, plot_raw, summarize_run
import numpy as np

run = open_run("<notebook_dir>/data/<file_id>")
print(summarize_run(run))
# expect: type 2D, recipe 'landau-fan', slow_param ['magnet_field'],
#         fast_param ['k_tg_volt', 'k_bg_volt'].
  suspended-device benchmark; expect a higher onset at lower quantum
  mobility, and read onset empirically in Step 3).
- **Luttinger sum.** Σf = n (g = 4) across the fan is the model-independent
  consistency check and the constraint that pins the global scale. A peak set
  that **cannot** satisfy the sum after the harmonic screen and stability
  sweep is a reportable state, not an extraction failure — R4G hosts
  documented non-Onsager regimes, though concentrated at large |D| / low n
  (survey §6); at the D ≈ 0 operating point treat it first as a degeneracy or
  N-assignment problem (audits above).
- **CNP magnitude is not a stacking read.** Insulating-CNP behavior has three
  candidate parents at N = 4 (survey §5) on top of the domain-shunting
  confound — feed it into the per-channel picture as consistent-with at
  most, never a standalone call.
- **Lever-arm / Nyquist at design time.** As in the trilayer sibling: ray
  slopes / frequencies must quantize against the (n, D) calibration; the
  B-axis SdH period sets the fan's B-row spacing — a fan failing the
  `landau-fan.md` Nyquist check in the claim window is uninformative there,
  re-measure.

            print(f"LEAK TRIP on {_gate.name} leg at V = {float(data[1]):+.3f} V: |I_swept| = {i_g:.3e}, |I_other| = {i_o:.3e} A")
            tripped.append((_gate.name, float(data[1]), i_g, i_o))
            station.interrupt_requested = True
    s.register_run_after(leak_guard, ())

    try:
        s.sweep(gate.volt, np.linspace(0, v_end, n_pts), delay=delay)
    finally:
        s.ramp(gate.volt, 0)
    if tripped:
        break

# CNP-line and D-line calibration

*Base recipe, rig-agnostic. Mostly analysis: it consumes the cooldown's
first 0 T gate map and produces the validated (n, D) conversion and the
constant-D line designer that every coordinate-claiming recipe downstream
(`landau-fan`, `nD-map`, feature positions) inherits. The house
conversion is the capacitance form — `sharpelab_nb.gates`:
`stack_capacitance` / `calc_nD` / `calc_gate_voltages` — with the
device's numbers in the device card. (The legacy thickness-parametrized
`calculate_n_D` is the single-dielectric special case of the same
helpers; older notebooks also carry inline equivalents — use those only
to replot their own runs.)*

## What
From a 0 T gate map: locate the charge-neutrality ridge per channel, fit
the CNP line in (V_tg, V_bg), refine the gate-capacitance **ratio** from
its slope (a fitted CNP slope dV_tg/dV_bg *is* −c_bg/c_tg), set the
density offset from its intercept, and emit constant-D gate-voltage
lines clipped to the validators. Output is a calibration contract
written to the device card: per-channel fits, the chosen (c_tg, c_bg)
with provenance split — **ratio: data-calibrated; absolute scale:
geometry prior until a quantum-Hall lever-arm check upgrades it** — the
offsets, a residual quality number, and the D-line designer parameters.

## When
After `gate-range-finding` (validators committed) and a first `gatemap`
that shows the CNP crossing the swept window. Re-run when:
- the operating point of a screening gate changes (the CNP intercept
  shifts with it; the slope usually survives — verify, don't assume);
- `reentry-baseline` shows feature-position drift across a handover;
- quantum-Hall data lands and enables the lever-arm upgrade (step 5).

No new sweeps are required if the gatemap is adequate; if the CNP exits
the window or is clipped (step 1 guard), this recipe specifies the map
extension and hands back to `gatemap`.

## Why
Every (n, D)-coordinate claim downstream inherits this calibration:
wrong capacitances tilt a fan's co-swept fast axis (the "fixed D" line
silently varies in D), shift every filling-factor assignment, and move
feature positions between sessions. The CNP slope is the cheapest
precise calibration in the corpus — one polyfit on a map you already
have — and it measures exactly the quantity the conversion needs
(c_bg/c_tg). What it does **not** measure is the absolute scale: slope
and intercept are invariant under c → λc, so n and D magnitudes carry
the geometry prior's uncertainty until ray slopes (dn/dB = ν·e/h) or
SdH frequencies pin the scale. Keep the two tiers separate in every
write-back; an absolute-n claim quoted at ratio-grade precision is a
provenance error (STYLE rule 5).

## Recipe

**Step 0 — inputs.** Re-form the gate map from the TSV per channel
(`plot.png` is the live monitor, not the measurement), with the device
card's channel arithmetic — including any mandatory gain division on the
current channel. Pull the dielectric-stack prior from the card and form
prior capacitances: `c = stack_capacitance([(t_nm, kappa), ...])` per
gate (series stacks — e.g. hBN over SiO₂ — are first-class).

**Step 1 — extract the CNP ridge, per channel.** For each four-terminal
channel separately (a 2T argmax is pulled off the CNP by contact features
and the V_bg≈0 stripe; never average channels — on a mosaic device the
channels disagree and the disagreement is signal, not noise): along each
gate-map row, locate the Rxx maximum across the fast axis. Smooth before
argmax when noisy (a 1D gaussian along the fast axis is the corpus
idiom). Three guards:
- **edge-clipped rows**: a row whose maximum sits at the swept-window
  edge has not located the CNP — exclude it from the fit and report the
  surviving row coverage; many clipped rows means the map is inadequate
  (see When).
- **competing maxima**: away from the CNP, contact-driven features or
  secondary peaks can outrun the CNP maximum. Restrict the argmax to a
  window around the visually-continuous ridge, or enforce continuity
  row-to-row; a ridge that jumps discontinuously is two features, not
  one line.
- **railed / glitch rows**: a 4T channel can rail at its sensitivity
  ceiling along a gapped CNP, flat-topping the argmax. Fit robustly —
  iterative outlier rejection (drop rows >~2σ off the line and refit)
  recovers the slope from the surviving rows; report the surviving
  coverage.

**Step 2 — fit, per channel.** Linear fit (`np.polyfit`) of ridge
position vs row coordinate; report slope and intercept per channel with
fit residuals. **State the axis orientation with the fit**: the
`c_bg/c_tg = −slope` reading in step 3 assumes the ridge position is
V_tg (fast axis) fitted against V_bg rows — a transposed map yields the
*inverted* ratio (e.g. 1.3 ↔ 0.77) with no other symptom until the
Verify geometry check; name which gate was which axis in the write-back. Read the residuals before trusting the line: structured
curvature (quantum capacitance, screening nonlinearity) makes a linear
slope window-dependent — if present, fit over the operating window the
campaign will actually use and say so. Cross-channel check: slopes
agreeing to a few percent → one calibration for the device *(heuristic
threshold — n = 1 device to date; better: compare the disagreement
against the per-channel fit residuals and say which bound you used)*;
disagreement beyond that is real spatial variation — keep per-channel
calibrations, flag it, and carry the channel question forward (it feeds
channel triage in the stacking/feature recipes; this recipe records the
disagreement, it does not interpret it).

**Step 3 — update the conversion.** From the chosen fit:
- **ratio**: `c_bg/c_tg = −slope`. Hold the better-constrained gate's
  capacitance at its stack prior and set the other from the ratio
  (heuristic — usually the simple single-dielectric gate is the anchor;
  state which you anchored).
- **density offset**: choose `n_offset` so the fitted line maps to
  n = 0: with `b` the V_tg intercept at V_bg = 0,
  `n_offset = -calc_nD(b, 0, c_tg, c_bg)[0]`.
- **D offset**: leave 0 unless the device exhibits a feature that
  physically locates D = 0 (e.g. a symmetric response in ±D); if you
  set it, cite the feature. An unexamined D_offset = 0 is itself a

class SdhTone:
    """One SdH tone's onset track from the matched-filter walk.

    `snr`/`amp` are per-window curves over `b_centers` (high-B → low-B). The
    filter is a Gaussian-windowed complex correlation at fixed `freq` whose
    FWHM spans `n_periods` periods of that tone (support `win_invB` in 1/B);
    SNR is amplitude over the record's white-noise floor, so a light tone and
    a heavy tone are each judged in their own natural window.
    """

    freq: float               # tone frequency, Tesla (record-resolution FFT)
    contrast: float           # tone-ID peak over the record spectral floor
    onset_b: float            # low-B onset, Tesla (record low edge if censored)
    censored: bool            # still above threshold in the lowest window
    revived: bool             # above-threshold windows exist below the walk stop
    marginal: bool            # peak SNR < marginal_mult x threshold everywhere
    near_residual: bool       # filter passband overlaps the detrend-residual band
    n_periods: float          # filter FWHM in periods (shrunk if record short)
    win_invB: float           # filter support width, 1/T
    harmonic_of: float | None  # freq of the lower tone this sits at ~k x of (fund.)
    harmonics: tuple[float, ...]  # freqs of tones that sit at ~k x of this one
    b_centers: np.ndarray     # per-window center field, descending (n_win,)
    snr: np.ndarray           # matched-filter SNR per window (n_win,)
    amp: np.ndarray           # matched-filter amplitude per window, Ohm-units

    def delta_f(self, b_max: float) -> float:
        """FFT resolution δF = 1/(1/onset_b − 1/b_max) over this tone's usable
        record — the per-tone version of the landau-fan design number."""
        return 1.0 / (1.0 / self.onset_b - 1.0 / b_max)


@dataclass
class SdhOnset:
    """Per-tone SdH onsets over the usable field window.

    `onset_b` is the headline: the lowest onset over non-marginal tracked
    tones — the low-B edge of usable oscillation content, which is the
    `landau-fan` step-1 `B_lo` contract (a light tone alive below the dominant
    tone's edge carries it). Everything behind it is in `tones` (per-tone
    onsets, SNR curves, censored/revived/marginal flags) and `untracked`
    (tones seen in the record-wide FFT but not trackable, with reasons).
    `summary()` renders the whole read for a notebook cell.
    """

    onset_b: float                       # min onset over robust tones, Tesla
    onset_freq: float                    # freq of the tone carrying onset_b
    clip_high_b: float                   # high edge of the analyzed window
    b_lo_record: float                   # low-B edge of the analyzed record
    noise_sigma: float                   # per-sample white-noise sigma used
    tones: list[SdhTone]                 # tracked tones, by contrast desc
    untracked: list[tuple[float, str]]   # (freq, reason) for untrackable tones

    @property
    def consensus_freq(self) -> float:
        """Dominant (highest-contrast) tone frequency, Tesla."""
        return self.tones[0].freq

    @property
    def b_centers(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """Dominant tone's window centers (see `tones` for the rest)."""
        return self.tones[0].b_centers

    @property
    def snr(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """Dominant tone's SNR curve (see `tones` for the rest)."""
        return self.tones[0].snr

    def summary(self) -> str:
        """Multi-line read for a notebook cell: headline, per-tone table,
        untracked tones with reasons."""
        carrier = f"tone {self.onset_freq:.1f} T"
        lines = [
            f"sdh_onset: onset_b = {self.onset_b:.2f} T ({carrier}) over "
            f"B [{self.b_lo_record:.2f}, {self.clip_high_b:.2f}] T"
        ]
        for t in self.tones:
            flags = [f for f, on in (("censored@edge", t.censored),
                                     ("revives-below-gap", t.revived),
                                     ("marginal", t.marginal),
                                     ("near-residual", t.near_residual)) if on]
            if t.harmonic_of is not None:
                k = t.freq / t.harmonic_of
                flags.append(f"~{k:.0f}x{t.harmonic_of:.1f}T")
            for fh in t.harmonics:
                flags.append(f"{round(fh / t.freq):.0f}x->{fh:.1f}T")
            tag = f"  [{', '.join(flags)}]" if flags else ""
            lines.append(
                f"  tone {t.freq:6.1f} T: onset {t.onset_b:5.2f} T  "
                f"dF {t.delta_f(self.clip_high_b):5.2f} T  "
                f"snr_max {np.nanmax(t.snr):6.1f}{tag}"
            )
        for f_t, reason in self.untracked:
            lines.append(f"  tone {f_t:6.1f} T: UNTRACKED — {reason}")

# `sweep` (measureme) API Reference

The measurement layer: `lib/measureme`, imported as `import sweep`. A
`Station` collects QCoDeS parameters to follow, runs 0D–2D sweeps, and writes
each run to a directory (`data.tsv.gz` + `metadata.json`) via a `Writer`.

Source: `sweep/sweep.py`, `sweep/db.py`. `import sweep` re-exports the
`sweep.sweep` surface (`from .sweep import *`); `sweep.db`, `sweep.raster`,
`sweep.sweep_load` are submodules.

---

## Station

### `Station(measurement_config=None, basedir=None, verbose=True)`
A collection of followed parameters with sweep methods. `measurement_config`
is an arbitrary dict stamped into every run's `metadata.json` (channel→contact,
gains, bias, …). `basedir` is the run-directory root; falls back to the module
`BASEDIR` (see `set_basedir`) then `os.getcwd()`. The station writes `log.log`
into `basedir`, so the directory must exist before construction.

### `AsyncStation(measurement_config=None, basedir=None, verbose=True)`
Subclass of `Station`, same constructor and identical I/O / data layout. Reads
are parallelized per-instrument (one thread per distinct instrument, one
executor reused across a sweep), and same-instrument parameters are
batch-read when supported — SR830 `snap` (`SnapReadable`, ≤6 params) or
SR86x `get_values` (`BatchReadable`, ≤3 params), else sequential. Use this by
default; it produces byte-identical output to `Station`.

### `follow_param(param, gain=1.0)` → `Station` · alias **`fp`**
Append a QCoDeS parameter to the followed list. The stored column value is
**`param() / gain`** (gain division happens at read time). Returns the station,
so calls chain: `s.fp(sr0.X, gain).fp(sr0.P)`. For a true-current channel
follow it with `gain=1`. Column name is `param.full_name`.

### `add_comment(comment)`
Append a comment to `metadata['comments']`. **Comments are station-lifetime**:
every comment added since construction lands in every subsequent run's
metadata — rebuild (or otherwise reset) the station between runs of different
intent. `metadata['comments'][0]` is conventionally the recipe slug.

### `ramp(param, setpoint)`
Logged direct set — calls `param(setpoint)`. It does **not** sub-step; smooth
ramping is the driver's own `step`/`inter_delay` (or a driver `ramp_*` method).

### `register_run_before(fn, args)` / `register_run_after(fn, args)`
Register a hook called at each measured point. `args` must be a tuple. The hook
is called `fn(*args, **context)` where **context is injected by parameter
name** (via `inspect.signature` — the hook receives only the context keys it
declares):

| context key | available in | value |
|---|---|---|
| `station` | before & after | the `Station` |
| `writer` | before & after | the active `sweep.db.Writer` |
| `data` | after only | the most recent data row (list) |

A hook whose parameter is named `station` gets it from context — passing it in
`args` too double-binds (`TypeError: multiple values for 'station'`). Order any
`args`-supplied params before the context ones. Keyword-only hook params can't
be set positionally via `args`; bind them with `functools.partial` (signature
is seen through the partial, so injection still works).

### Other methods
- `measure()` → `SweepResult` — single 0D point.
- `watch(delay=0.0, max_duration=None)` → `SweepResult` — repeat-measure over
  time until `max_duration` (or interrupt).
- `read(param, gain=1.0)` / `read_all()` — log a one-off read, no run written.
- `plot(x, y, z=None)` / `reset_plots()` — live monitor only, not the data.
- `reset()` — clear the interrupted flag so the station can sweep again.

---

## Sweeps

Each sweep method returns a `SweepResult` and writes one run directory. The
**data-row column layout** is fixed per method (and matches `metadata['columns']`).
`*followed` is the followed-parameter values in `fp` order, each already
gain-divided.

| method | signature | row layout |
|---|---|---|
| `measure` | `()` | `[time, *followed]` |
| `watch` | `(delay=0.0, max_duration=None)` | `[time, *followed]` |
| `sweep` | `(param, setpoints, delay=0.0)` | `[time, setpoint, *followed]` |
| `multisweep` | `(params, setpointslist, delay=0.0)` | `[time, *setpoints, *followed]` |
| `megasweep` | `(slow_param, slow_v, fast_param, fast_v, slow_delay=0.0, fast_delay=0.0, init_delay=True)` | `[time, slow, fast, *followed]` |
| `multimegasweep` | `(slow_params, slow_v_list, fast_params, fast_v_list, slow_delay=0.0, fast_delay=0.0, init_delay=True)` | `[time, *slow, *fast, *followed]` |

- **`sweep`** — 1D. Sets `param` to each setpoint, waits `delay`, measures.
- **`multisweep`** — 1D, several parameters **co-swept**. `params` and
  `setpointslist` are parallel lists; `setpointslist[i]` is the vector for
  `params[i]`, and **all vectors must be equal length** (raises otherwise). At
  point j every `params[i]` is set to `setpointslist[i][j]` — one path through
  N-space, not a grid (e.g. a fixed-D (Vtg, Vbg) line).
- **`megasweep`** — 2D grid: outer `slow_param` over `slow_v`, inner
  `fast_param` over `fast_v`. `slow_delay` waits once per slow row (at the first
  fast point), `fast_delay` waits at every point.
- **`multimegasweep`** — 2D grid where each axis is a **co-swept bundle**.
  `slow_params`/`slow_v_list` and `fast_params`/`fast_v_list` are parallel

## Runs 6–7 — spot-check read before the Landau fan

Raw signed resistance first, then onset/FFT stability. Only sr1 (B_1–B_2, source T_0/drain B_3) probes a wired voltage pair. Run 6 is electron n=+3.2×10¹² cm⁻², run 7 hole n=−1.2×10¹², both D≈0 on the run-5 ridge-A calibration. Nominal Luttinger frequencies are 33.09 and 12.41 T; absolute density remains a geometry prior. The second CNP ridge gives a possible +0.43×10¹² density offset along the same contact path, not an independently resolved region.

**Read:** both runs are complete, conductive and unclipped. Electron peaks recur near 7.3, 14.7, 22.2, 29.5 T (roughly a harmonic series); the hole peak set shifts more with extraction window and is confined to the near-CNP regime where the ABAB pair is close. Neither is a classification-grade partition yet. In particular, do not label the 29.5 T tone ABCA, or automatically discard the 22 T component as a harmonic. The next measurement is the electron fan to test frequency trajectories and reproduce on a different sampling grid. Negative signed R minima and the series-path/mosaic possibility remain explicit caveats.

**Onset fork:** full 0.3–10 T polynomial subtraction makes the electron onset censored at 0.3 T; those low-field points also undersample the fastest tone (50 mT below 1 T). Restricting background estimation to ≤4 T removes the large high-field MR upturn: "'`sdh_onset(..., b_hi=4, bg_degree=5)` returns 1.03091 T, carried by 6.7 T. Degree 3 retains that tone at 1.04 T but flags it marginal and assigns the robust headline to the 22 T component at 1.38 T. Use 1.03091 T as the exploratory fan edge, carry 1.0–1.4 T onset uncertainty, and do not turn a missing partner into exclusion without verifying its usable record. Hole onset is ~0.71–0.75 T, but its allowed D=0 density never reaches the ≥2–3×10¹² discriminating window.

The fan interpretation must compare a shared +3.2 column to run 6, screen harmonics with density dependence and the full Luttinger sum, fit one global density scale, and overlay both ABAB and adjacent-N trilayer curves. A final strong call may need LK/F_L-origin work; this fan is the next evidence step, not a promised verdict. References: `sdh-spot-check`, `landau-fan-vti`, `tetralayer-stacking-fs-count` Steps 2–5 and Verify.

def assert_thermometry_live(
    name: str,
    paths: str | Sequence[str],
    *,
    max_age: float,
    max_period: float | None = None,
    ts_index: int = 0,
) -> str:
    """Bring-up liveness gate on worker logfiles — raise, don't warn.

    Gates the **freshest** candidate (the other probe's file is legitimately
    stale): its last line must be younger than ``max_age`` seconds (dead or
    hung worker), and, when ``max_period`` is given, the spacing of its last
    two lines must not exceed it (a live worker at the wrong cadence, e.g. a
    legacy publisher). Prints the passing readback and returns the path.

    Complements `temperature_from_logfiles`, whose per-get staleness is a
    deliberately non-fatal warning sized for mid-sweep reads — this is the
    hard gate for the setup cell, run before anything trusts a T readback.
    """
    candidates = [paths] if isinstance(paths, str) else list(paths)
    now = time.time()
    best: tuple[float, float | None, str] | None = None  # (age, period, path)
    errors: list[str] = []
    for p in candidates:
        try:
            lines = _read_last_lines(p)
            ts = float(lines[-1][ts_index])
            age = now - ts
            period = ts - float(lines[-2][ts_index]) if len(lines) > 1 else None
        except (OSError, ValueError, IndexError) as e:
            errors.append(f"{os.path.basename(p)}: {e}")
            continue
        if best is None or age < best[0]:
            best = (age, period, p)
    if best is None:
        raise TimeoutError(
            f"{name}: no readable thermometry logfile in {candidates} ({errors})"
        )
    age, period, path = best
    base = os.path.basename(path)
    if age > max_age:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"{name}: freshest logfile ({base}) is {age:.0f}s old "
            f"(gate {max_age:.0f}s) — worker dead or hung; fix before measuring"
        )
    if max_period is not None and period is not None and period > max_period:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"{name}: {base} writes every {period:.0f}s (gate {max_period:.0f}s) "
            f"— wrong worker cadence; redeploy the worker"
        )
    detail = f", period {period:.0f}s" if period is not None else ""
    print(f"{name}: {base} live — age {age:.0f}s{detail}")
    return path

## HERA — electron Landau fan for the stacking investigation

"'`landau-fan-vti` under `tetralayer-stacking-fs-count` Step 4. Gate C passed (runs 0–3); run 5 locates the CNP and D≈0 line. Spot checks 6/7 are now analyzed in ana cells 14–15: electron frequency components near 7.3/14.7/22.2/29.5 T are more reproducible than the near-CNP hole spectrum, but their harmonic/pocket identities remain unresolved. This fan measures their density trajectories and repeats +3.2 on a changed field grid. Only B_1–B_2 is wired; the two CNP ridges within that path are a spatial-inhomogeneity confound, not two separately measurable regions.

**Design and resolution.** D=0 in the same run-6 rounded calibration (ratio data-calibrated, scale geometry-prior). n=+2.8…+3.2×10¹² cm⁻², 10 paired gate points; TG +0.869016…+0.983621 V, BG +1.017844…+1.166125 V, Si unchanged at 0. B=1.0309096914→7.05 T, 238 rows uniform in 1/B. `sdh_onset(run6, b_hi=4, bg_degree=5)` supplies B_lo; the full 10 T fit is background-sensitive/censored, and degree 3 makes the ~7 T tone marginal (robust headline 1.38 T). This onset fork is carried explicitly: do not infer partner absence from the nominal full window alone.

Model `fs_count_b0.abab_fs` predicts (light,heavy) = (6.038,22.914), (6.673,24.351), (7.306,25.783) T at n=2.8,3.0,3.2; ABCA F_L=28.950…33.085 T. The nominal inverse-field span is 0.82817 T⁻¹, δF=1.2075 T, five periods of the smallest nominal ABAB partner, and heavy/singleton separation ≥6.04 T >2δF. A higher actual onset or a lower global density scale reduces that period count; it limits confidence rather than licensing a hidden redefinition of the window. Δn=0.04444×10¹² gives 2.24 samples per g=4 ray at B_lo (floor N_n=10). Δ(1/B)=0.0034944 T⁻¹ gives Nyquist 143.09 T: although F_L alone permits coarser sampling, run 6 tracks higher components through ~130 T and a coarser fan would alias them into putative pockets. N_B=238 is the floor at the chosen 0.0035 spacing. The +3.2 column must reproduce run 6 before a new frequency claim is trusted.

**Coverage trade.** This is the high-electron discriminating slice.
